title: Bitcoin and ether rebound, DeFi access expands, portfolio reaches $52,600
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $60,624, up 3.5% over 24 hours, while ether rose 3.7% to about $1,698. The broader market was less convincing: CoinGecko put total crypto capitalization near $2.07 trillion, essentially unchanged. The recovery in the two largest assets therefore sits alongside a flatter aggregate market, with no clear evidence yet of a uniform rebound across crypto.

US inflation remains a constraint on the outlook. The latest BEA release put annual headline PCE inflation at 3.8% and core inflation at 3.3%; both measures rose 0.3% over the month. Real consumer spending was essentially flat. For crypto, persistent inflation matters because it can limit the scope for easier monetary policy and keep financing conditions restrictive. Those figures provide macro context, without establishing what caused every move in token prices.

The European Banking Authority published a report examining stablecoins in decentralized finance. It highlighted their use as collateral and settlement assets, alongside risks that DeFi arrangements could bypass MiCA requirements, including restrictions on interest paid on e-money tokens. The EBA wants the European Commission to consider additional requirements for firms providing access to DeFi, especially lending. This is a recommendation for regulatory review, with potential consequences for how European customers reach those services.

Franklin Templeton filed a prospectus supplement saying its EZPZ crypto index ETF will add Hyperliquid's HYPE on or about December 1. HYPE joins seven existing assets as the underlying index changes, with quarterly rebalancing continuing. The addition broadens exposure available through a brokerage account. The filing does not specify the size of the purchase, so it provides no basis for a firm demand estimate.

Aave Labs also opened its savings app to the public after reporting more than $63 million in early-access balances. Bank connections and simplified accounts aim to make lending markets easier to use. Borrower interest funds the underlying returns. The app's advertised launch rate is variable, and balances are not bank deposits covered by FDIC or SIPC protection. Easier access leaves the economic and technical risks of lending in place.

Our on-chain portfolio totals about $52,637: $8,769 in the active treasury and $43,868 in the Safe. That is $2,098, or 4.2%, above the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC balances are unchanged and worth about $36,250, nearly 69% of net portfolio value. The Safe also holds a $5,203 WETH/ARC pool, adding further ARC exposure. Beefy positions total $1,672, while Curve is up from $308 to $435.

Aave borrowing totals about $3,155 against $5,832 of supplied WETH. Health factors improved from 1.70 to 1.77 in the treasury and from 1.36 to 1.41 in the Safe, although falling ether prices would reduce those cushions. Fluid remains the tightest lending risk: roughly $156 net value, $1,067 debt and a 1.03 health factor. Its supplied balance mix shifted toward USDC and away from syrupUSDC. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk.
